item.title: Bawnboy native appointed Bishop of Killala
item.description: Archbishop of Tuam Francis Duffy has been appointed as the Bishop of Killala. The Co Cavan native has been holding the position of Apostolic Administrator of Killala for almost two years before his recent appointment. The decision results in the Diocese of Killala and the Archdiocese of Tuam being united under the same Bishop. Advertisement It paves the way for the formal amalgamation of the two dioceses.

item.title: Monaghan Camogs off to a winning start
item.description: Monaghan Camogs made a winning return back to inter-county level after a 15 year break when they overcame Donegal on Saturday in Carndonagh in Division 3B of the league. The 2 and a half hour journey coupled with tough weather conditions and heavy playing condtions didn't deter the farney side as they led by 4-3 to 3-4 at the break. item.title: Fundraiser underway for memorial to Cavan orphanage victims
item.description: A Go Fund Me page has been set up as part of ongoing efforts to have a memorial erected at the site of the Orphanage fire disaster in Cavan. The Cavan Orphanage Memorial Committee have launched the fundraiser in a bid to have a memorial in situ to remember the 34 children and one adult that lost their lives. item.title: Irish language organisation passes historic motion surrounding Irish unity
item.description: Local councillor Stiofán Conaty has welcomed the development by Conradh na Gaeilge which have voted to amend its constitution to work towards Irish Unity. He described it as "hugely significant and a historic development". Cllr Conaty said he was proud to attend Ard-Fheis Chonradh na Gaeilge in Belfast, where delegates from across the island voted overwhelmingly in favour of the amendment. item.title: Open drug dealing in Monaghan - "we can't normalise this kind of behaviour"
item.description: A local councillor has highlighted the issue surrounding open drug dealing in Monaghan Town. Cllr Alan Johnson brought a motion to the Monaghan Municipal District meeting surrounding anti-social behaviour. The local councillor said while it's a very small number of people it was something that needed to be highlighted in an effort to eradicate the problem.
